entry.evidence: uncertainties over the sources of this material prevent understanding of the precise causes of this greatly enhanced atmospheric dustiness

steps.action: Frame the open question of whether northern ice sheets and their meltwater pulses supplied the sediment that drove MIS 2 dust activity and loess formation in NW Europe.
steps.quote: In sum, the role of northern ice sheets in dust generation and loess formation is debated

steps.action: Take from the authors' earlier luminescence dating at Pegwell Bay two phases of greatly enhanced dust accumulation (25-23.5 ka and 20-19 ka) that coincide with North Sea Lobe advances and retreats.
steps.quote: two phases of greatly enhanced accumulation that match the timing of advances and retreats of nearby ice lobes in the North Sea

steps.action: Review the published rival source scenarios: BIIS-derived glacigenic material, FIS/Scandinavian material, Alpine material carried by the Rhine, the local Thanet Formation, and a temporal shift from local to glacial sources.
steps.quote: a wide range of possible proto-sources and transport pathways for meltwater sediment, dust and loess in southeast England remains plausible

steps.action: Design the test as a multi-proxy provenance study (zircon U-Pb, bulk Nd, heavy minerals, quartz SEM) of dated ice-marginal loess against potential source sediments and protosource terranes.
steps.quote: SE England represents an ideal test of the contested role of northern ice sheets in loess and dust generation

steps.action: Select loess samples from the previously dated Pegwell Bay section and collect reference samples (Thanet Fm, Skipsea and Basement tills, Dogger lake core 155VC, modern Rhine).
steps.quote: we collected 5 reference samples from potential dust source sediments

steps.action: Compile published detrital and igneous zircon U-Pb ages from European basement terranes and published data from Cenozoic North Sea sediments.
steps.quote: In order to retrace protosources of potential dust source sediments in the North Sea region and loess in southeast England

steps.action: Measure large-n detrital zircon U-Pb ages by LA-ICPMS, automated heavy-mineral assemblages (TIMA), bulk Nd isotopes, and SEM quartz grain shape and surface textures on the loess and reference samples.
steps.quote: we generated large n data sets (aiming for >300 analyzed grains)

steps.action: Check the Nd isotope measurements against the JNDi-1, BCR-2 and AGV-2 reference standards, which agree with their recommended and certified values.
steps.quote: in full agreement with the recommended value of 0.512115

steps.action: Compare the loess zircon spectra with terrane and source-sediment spectra (KDE, MDS): the upper loess is consistent with British (possibly Scandinavian) basement, while the lower loess adds a Variscan/Continental European component.
steps.quote: indicate temporal variability in protosource assemblages

steps.action: Add bulk Nd isotopes to counter the possible over-representation of proximal sources in zircon data caused by gravitational sorting; loess eNd falls between Continental fluvial and BIIS/FIS glacigenic values.
steps.quote: we complement the zircon age framework with bulk Nd isotope data

steps.action: Find that crustal-age proxies cannot exclude the Thanet Fm or Neogene western North Sea sediments as sources.
steps.quote: may not be sufficient to discriminate between potential source sediments for loess in southeast England

steps.action: Turn to heavy-mineral maturity (ZTR) and quartz microtextures as further methods to separate the candidate source sediments.
steps.quote: Analysis of heavy mineral assemblages and quartz grain morphology from loess and potential source sediments provides a means to further differentiate

steps.action: Exclude the Thanet Fm and pre-glacial Neogene North Sea sediments as major sources, citing the high Thanet Fm ZTR and glacial-grinding fracture marks on the loess quartz.
steps.quote: the striking differences in heavy mineral composition make these sands unlikely as a major source for the overlying Pegwell Bay loess

steps.action: Answer the mismatch (the tills lack the Variscan/Cadomian grains seen in the loess; ZTR values differ) by invoking till heterogeneity, glacially recycled sandstones and post-depositional weathering, keeping a BIIS source.
steps.quote: glacial till deposits are heterogeneous by definition

steps.action: Pose a rival account of the lower-loess Variscan/Cadomian grains: Continental European fluvial sediment, supported by quartz morphology and by Milodowski et al. at Ospringe.
steps.quote: An alternative explanation for the origins of the Variscan to Cadomian age zircon grains detected in the lower loess sample

steps.action: Note that the uniform eNd through time conflicts with the temporal provenance change, and propose an additional FIS input that would average out the Nd signal.
steps.quote: this temporal change in Pegwell Bay loess provenance recorded by zircon age assemblages and quartz grain morphology seems to contradict

steps.action: Exclude the Rhine as a source of the lower loess on heavy-mineral differences (zircon, rutile, tourmaline, hornblende, olivine), while noting that dilution by mixing could hide it and more data are needed.
steps.quote: suggesting that the Rhine is not a source to the lower loess at Pegwell Bay

steps.action: Keep the claim that the upper loess is entirely BIIS-derived and the lower loess is BIIS-dominated, with a plausible mixed FIS/Central European addition.
steps.quote: the upper loess sample at Pegwell Bay seems entirely BIIS derived

steps.action: Build a model linking North Sea Lobe retreat, Dogger lake drainage and meltwater routing to the two loess phases and to the expected source mixtures (Fig. 9).
steps.quote: Mixed glaciofluvial and lake sediments released during this event potentially included particles derived from protosources in Britain, Scandinavia and Continental Europe

steps.action: Compare the model's expected sources with the sample ages and provenance: mixed grains in the lower loess and near-absence of Variscan grains in the upper loess, consistent with BIIS supply after the 20 ka NSL collapse.
steps.quote: the new provenance data suggest that the resultant, sudden availability of BIIS derived sediment acted as source

steps.action: Check the timing against independent Bay of Biscay marine core records (Fe/Ca, Ti/Ca, turbidite flux) of terrigenous input coincident with both loess phases.
steps.quote: marine sediment cores from the Bay of Biscay at the western outlet of the Channel (Fig. 1) also record increased terrigenous sediment input

steps.action: Keep the claim that episodic loess deposition in SE England was controlled mainly by ice-dynamics-driven sediment availability in the southern North Sea.
steps.quote: episodic loess deposition over southeast England is primarily a function of sediment availability in the southern North Sea

steps.action: Extend the model to the EIS margin more widely, arguing that a loess preservation bias makes the ice-sheet dust contribution look smaller than it was.
steps.quote: We propose that the record of dust activity in this loess caused by increased sediment availability in the proglacial zone may be widely representative

steps.action: State a new hypothesis, left for future testing, that abrupt climate, dust and ocean events of the last glacial are linked through ice-sheet drainage dynamics.
steps.quote: we hypothesize that the observed abrupt climate, dust, and oceanographic events of the last glacial phase

end.claim: Multi-proxy provenance evidence shows that ice-sheet (chiefly BIIS) derived material dominated the sources of MIS 2 loess in SE England, and North Sea ice-margin dynamics drove episodic proglacial sediment supply and dust deposition.

decisive_move.sentence: Heavy-mineral maturity and glacial-grinding quartz microtextures exclude the Thanet Fm and pre-glacial North Sea sediments, which crustal-age proxies alone could not separate, so the ice-sheet source claim depends on this exclusion.

gates.evidence: The ice-sheet test framing directed the choice of reference samples (tills, Dogger lake core, Rhine, Thanet Fm), but the loess section and its chronology were inherited. The glacial-source claim could have failed (e.g. a Thanet Fm match), yet mismatches (Variscan grains absent from the tills, ZTR differences, uniform Nd) were absorbed by auxiliary arguments. No pre-registration or fixed thresholds are reported beyond standard discordance filters.

novelty_claims.quote: which not only provide new insight into both loess source
Multi-proxy evidence allows us to unambiguously identify ice sheet derived sediments in the exposed North Sea basin as the dominant source of loess
This implies the role of ice sheets in controlling wider dust emission may be underestimated.

limits: Zircon, heavy-mineral and SEM data come from only two loess samples (Nd from ten), so the temporal provenance contrast rests on two points. Quartz microtextures are described qualitatively, and no quantitative mixing or unmixing model is reported. The Rhine exclusion is tentative, and the authors call for more data. Coincidence of loess phases with ice-margin retreat rests on published chronologies, including the authors' own earlier dating. No review file was supplied, so the effect of the two acknowledged reviewers cannot be coded (inference). Calling the glacial-source claim a best explanation rather than confirmed is the coder's inference: the till-representativeness and weathering arguments protect the hypothesis rather than test it. Sub-claims: the upper loess being BIIS-derived is best_explanation; the lower-loess mixed FIS/Central European contribution is left open by the authors; the wider EIS preservation-bias and dust-climate coupling claims are stated as hypotheses requiring testing (no status).

disagreements.target: Local derivation of Thanet loess from the Thanet Formation (Pitcher et al., 1954; Catt et al., 1987; Milodowski et al., 2015)
disagreements.support: Thanet Fm sands have a much higher ZTR than the loess and lack glacial-grinding quartz textures.
disagreements.quote: the striking differences in heavy mineral composition make these sands unlikely as a major source for the overlying Pegwell Bay loess

disagreements.target: Rhine-borne Alpine source for North Sea loess (Smalley et al., 2009)
disagreements.support: The modern Rhine heavy-mineral assemblage (zircon, rutile, tourmaline, hornblende, olivine) differs from the loess, though mixing could mask the difference.
disagreements.quote: suggesting that the Rhine is not a source to the lower loess at Pegwell Bay

disagreements.target: Scandinavian origin of SE England loess suggested by amphiboles (Eden, 1980)
disagreements.support: Zircon ages and Nd point to an entirely BIIS-derived upper loess, with a possible FIS contribution only to the lower loess.
disagreements.quote: the upper loess sample at Pegwell Bay seems entirely BIIS derived

disagreements.target: Toucanne et al. (2015) attribution of Channel meltwater pulses to FIS recession
disagreements.support: Pegwell Bay provenance and timing point to localized North Sea Lobe controls on sediment supply.
disagreements.quote: Although Toucanne et al. (2015) dominantly attributed these meltwater pulses to FIS recession phases

disagreements.target: View that thin, intermittent NW European loess cover implies a minor ice-sheet role in dust production
disagreements.support: A preservation-bias argument (erosion along the ice-marginal spillway, submerged basins, reworking), supported by literature rather than new data.
disagreements.quote: this apparently generally thinner, intermittent loess coverage should not be taken as indicative of reduced dust activity compared to central Europe

disagreements.target: Importance of strong east-sector winds from the BIIS-FIS anticyclone for dust transport (Schaffernicht et al., 2020)
disagreements.support: Loess deposition continued after decoupling of the ice sheets, implying sediment availability rather than winds controlled near-source deposition.
disagreements.quote: such enhanced dust transporting winds were not critical for near source loess deposition
